 ::JUDGMENT:
:
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 07.11.2023 at about 2.00 a.m. had been driving his Toyota Etios Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AB- 7736 and stopped on Hosaguddadahalli Signal Junction, from City Market to KSRTC Junction, at that time, a Tamil Nadu Government Bus bearing Reg. No.TN-29-N- 2907 being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his car, due to which, his car was completely damaged.
3. The petitioner was working as a driver by owning a car and was earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.

Due to this accident, he has left his car for repair at Toyota Viva Magna Wheelers Pvt. Ltd., Mysuru Road,
Bengaluru and has spent a sum of Rs.2,38,450/-, out of which insurer has paid a sum of Rs.1,42,552/-.

entities.text: Toyota Viva Magna Wheelers Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further contended that, due to this accident, the vehicle was in garage for a SCCH-5 period of three months, hence he has lost his income for 3 months and he has incurred huge loss and availed loan of Rs.1,00,000/- for maintenance of the family.
4. The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Tamil Nadu Bus and Byhatarayanapura traffic Police have registered a case in Cr. NO.395/2023 under Sec.279 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 is driver of the said offending TNSTC Bus, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
5.
On service of notice, respondent No.1 being R.C.Owner of TNSTC has appeared and filed written statement denying averments of the petition.
Further submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioner SCCH-5 is speculative, imaginary and exorbitant.
Further denied occurrence of the accident, occupation and income of the petitioner, expenses incurred by the petitioner towards repair of the car etc., Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

No.KA-04-AB-7736 near Hosaguddadahalli junction, at that time, a driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.
No.TN-29-N-2907 driven in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car and caused damages to the same?
SCCH-5 2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. In order to prove her case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence by the respondents.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in his chief- SCCH-5 examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of police notice is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.8.

sentences.text: Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he has not examined any witness.

Further on perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., as FIR, complaint, sketch, spot mahazar,
charge sheet, police notice, reply and IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated SCCH-5 07.11.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondents have not not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of damages as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Hence I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the damages to the car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AB-7736 out of the accident held on 07.11.2023 at about 2.00 a.m. when he was stopping the car at signal near Hosaguddadahalli Junction, from city market to KSRTC junction.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the TNSTC SCCH-5 Bus bearing Reg. No.TN-29-N-2907.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioner, in the alleged accident, his Toyota Etios Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AB-7736 was completely damaged.

In this regard he has furnished copy of IMV Report marked as Ex.P.8 wherein it is clearly mentioned that, rear bumper, dickey door, wind shield glass damaged, rear both side wheel fender is damaged, rear right side tail lamp assembly damaged and rear right side chassis is bend.

Petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.2,38,450/- to get the car repaired, out of which his insurer has paid a sum SCCH-5 of Rs.1,42,552/- and remaining amount of Rs.95,898/- is paid by the petitioner by availing loan.
14. Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- to the loss of income during the period of repair of his car in the garage.
Contrary to the said facts, there is no contrary materials are placed by the respondents except filing of written statement.
Hence I have no hesitation to believe the petitioner case.
15. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,15,898/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

16. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the R.C.Owner and incharge of TNSTC is liable to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within SCCH-5 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
